summary: Session 2 of 2 (final) made the harvester's human-review step self-instructing and one-click. Authored docs/harvester/reviewing-the-feedback-artifacts.md (plain-language per-artifact developer guide: what each *-checklist.json / classification.json is, what the developer does, which zero-install editor opens it), added interpretation-guide §3.3 (mandatory AI-agent rule: explain each artifact + link the editor + copy-paste script, never hand over raw JSON), removed the stale 'forthcoming guide' promise from §3.1, and wired the editor URLs into the emitted READ-ME-FIRST.md template + both golden copies + docs index. Resolved the spec's editor-hosting open decision by cross-provider consensus (gpt-5-4 + gemini-pro, journaled in ai_router/consensus-decisions.jsonl): defer classification-editor GitHub Pages hosting (document local-open); confirm uat-checklist-editor for both checklists. Investigating open-decision (b) surfaced and fixed a real one-click-blocking bug: UsageChecklistWriter serialized object-use-checklist.json in camelCase, so it loaded as an EMPTY checklist in the PascalCase-only uat-checklist-editor; fixed the writer (split _camelOpts/_pascalOpts mirroring CleanupChecklistWriter), updated the unit test that had encoded the bug, and regenerated the two committed golden object-use-checklist.json samples via the hermetic identify-usage path (casing-only change, verified). Validated incrementally per a new lessons-learned tactic: solution build 0 errors; AccessHarvester.Pipeline.Tests (excl. COM probe) 684 passed/0 failed; the fragile Access-COM/PDF tier was intentionally not run since all changes are hermetic. Cross-provider verification (gpt-5-4) VERIFIED on round 1.

reason.specifics: Routed recommendation (gemini-pro, do-not-self-opine): start the sanitize-against-HomeHealthCare timeout investigative spike next — reliability before features, the ordering this arc just validated. Re-measure FIRST: the just-closed harvester-access-com-graceful-shutdown set hardened AccessComSession and may have resolved the timeout as a side effect, in which case the spike closes with a documentation note and no code work. No spec required (goal already documented in lessons-learned.md). harvester-sql-migration-generator is the capstone after, needs its own spec, and a belongs-here-vs-future-migration-repo check. The routed call suggested an ultra-cheap diagnostic model on pure cost grounds, but a sanitize/OLE-DB/COM diagnostic that must comprehend this repo's extraction code needs a capable model on a Windows+Access host; start at effort=low (cheap re-measure) and escalate only if the timeout reproduces.
